items.title: 67259_Big Chief Moore oral history interview
items.q: [INTERVIEWER] Yes, Don Byas was at a place called the Rinkside and Bill Coleman was around, too.

ctx.x: I see. Let's who else -- Was it Byas?

Yes, Don Byas was at a place called the Rinkside and Bill Coleman was around, too. Also I saw an advertisement, friend of mine, Huddie Ledbetter better known as Leadbelly and he was making an appearance at the University of Paris. And I went to the concert, well received, beautiful man, old man but he's still sharp. He's got a good voice and he was singing while he was there.
Did Paris audiences like the kind of blues singing that he did and his folk songs.

items.title: 71542_Bill Coleman autobiographical manuscript
items.q: The American musicians presented at this festival were Bechet, Parker, "Big Chief" Russell Moore, Oran "Hot Lips" Page, Kenny Dorham, Tommie Potter, Al Haig, Max Roach, Miles Davis, Jimmy McPartland, Ted Dameron, Kenny Clarke, Georges Johnson, James Moody, Richie Frost, Don Byas and myself.

ctx.x: The war had not changed naything in Kokke since I was there the summer of 1938. Everything went well until the last night when Don Byas went into one of his acts after the last show. Of course, we all had quite a few drinks and were feeling no pains. I had already left the casino when thiks incident happened, but I was told by one of the musicians that Don was high and in the process of changing his clothes, he decided to chase one of the Bluebell girls that had passed his lodge when the door was open. But he was…

The big thing in jazz from the 8th of May until the 15th was the jazz festival that Charles Delaunay organized in collaboration with Frank Bauer, Eddie Barclay and Jacques Souplet. Sidney Bechet and Charlie(the Bird) Parker were the stars, but there were other musicians that were already in the limelight, whose names were to become much better known than they were in 1949. The American musicians presented at this festival were Bechet, Parker, "Big Chief" Russell Moore, Oran "Hot Lips" Page, Kenny Dorham, Tommie…

Jazz was jumping in Paris that week at the Salle Pleyel and jazz fans from different countries (mostly those who had musicians that were favoured in the places they were from) were here to take in the festival and all the jazz clubs were jumping and especially the club St. Germain des Pres on the left bank of Paris, because the American musicians and some from other countries would go jamming after the nightly concerts or on nights when they did not have to appear with Rostaing(clarinet) Braslavsky(clarinet)…
